newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Oak up on gold reserve expansion.
newsitem.headline: Royal Oak up on gold reserve expansion.

text.p: Royal Oak Mines Inc attracted a lot of attention in morning trading in Toronto on Wednesday after the gold company said it had expanded its reserves at its Ontario exploration properties.
Shares in Royal Oak were up C$0.45 to C$5.45 in heavy trading of more than one million shares.
The Kirkland, Washington-based company said it had expanded its reserves at its gold properties in the Timmins area of Northern Ontario.
The company said the land contains 7.3 million ounces of gold in 132 million tons, grading 0.056 ounces per tonne.
The latest estimate increases reserves by 2.81 millioun ounces.
"It's shaping up quite nicely for them," said mining analyst Vahid Fathi with Everen Securities Inc.
The Ontario expansion, along with developments at the Kemess deposit in Canada's British Columbia, should help Royal Oak boost earnings and cut costs, said Fathi.
"These are the other pieces of the puzzle that are falling in place to put Royal Oak on the map as a low-cost producer," he said.
He put a long-term target of US$9 on the stock.
Royal Oak also trades on the American Stock Exchange. The stock was up 1/4 to 3-15/16 by midday on Wednesday.
The company is working on a feasibility study for open pit and underground mining, spokesman Graham Eacott said in an interview.

Production by late 1998 is expected to be about 300,000 ounces per year from the Timmins and Matachewan camps, with cash cstos at about US$225 an ounce. Costs in the area are about US$240 right now and about US$331 company wide, Eacott said.
But the numbers for development in Northern Ontario are far from final as the company continues to drill, Eacott added.
"We're very delighted with this increase of reserves and we expect with further drilling up to the end of this year that the figures will increase," he said.
Royal Oak aims to boost company-wide production from the current 415 million ounces a year to more than one million ounces a year by the year 2000, said Eacott.
He said Royal Oak has spent about C$9 million on exploration this year in the Timmins area.
